body: my question is that how to handle the user whic is removed from the group by administrator and the user didn't login in again
I would like to add a api that can update groups, then we can make a client(e.g. get uses' info from LDAP) to sync groups into headscale.

@IamTaoChen This PR does not address group synchronization between the idp and headscale dynamically. This was mentioned in my PRs description. That is a separate feature/issue and outside the scope of #2366. I am happy to do a follow up PR to address group synchronization, but this PR does not solve that. This PR only adds the functionality for group claims in the ACLs.

`Refresh model is snapshot-on-login. Groups update when the user re-authenticates against the IdP, not on a timer. Admins tune staleness tolerance via node.expiry. This is the "nothing dynamic, nothing fancy" model called for in [OIDC] Plans about Known limitation  #1121 and matches the acceptable trade-off kradalby outlined in [Feature] Support using groups from OIDC in ACLs #2366. Other refresh mechanisms discussed in the issue threads (offline-access + UserInfo polling, LDAP federation, SCIM v2 provisioning) all still need a place to persist the IdP's group claims for ACL evaluation — i.e. they would all build on the User.Groups storage and state.UpdateUser → Headscale.Change path this PR introduces, not replace it. Those approaches are out of scope here per kradalby's prior call. If there is appetite for any of these (SCIMv2, LDAP, etc) I'd be happy to work on them in separate PRs.`

@juanfont @bilbo-foo Are there any blockers (other than conflicts) keeping this initial implementation from being merged? Seems like a solid start, and I would be happy to contribute to further work on SCIM support for refresh after we get this in
Is there any update on this? I would be happy to help with testing (especially for SCIM later)

message:
types: add identity-provider group memberships

Model groups asserted by an identity provider as a Group entity and a
per-source UserGroup membership, loaded onto User through a read-only
association. Each source owns its memberships, so syncing one (the OIDC
groups claim at login) can never clobber another's.

QualifyGroupName normalises a provider group name into the
<name>@<domain> identifier that policies reference as
group:<name>@<domain>, matching Tailscale's syntax for synced groups.
Only ASCII letters are case folded (FoldGroupName): full Unicode folding
would merge distinct names such as the Kelvin sign with 'k'.

User.PolicyEqual now compares group names so a membership change
recompiles the policy instead of being skipped as unchanged, and
User.InGroup checks membership without allocating for the policy's
per-reference lookups.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

db: store identity-provider group memberships

Add the groups and user_groups tables with explicit DDL for SQLite and
Postgres, created by a migration and by InitSchema. Memberships cascade
when their user or group is deleted, and user_groups.source is not
CHECK-constrained so a new source needs no table rebuild.

SetUserGroups replaces one source's memberships for a user in a
transaction and reports whether they changed; an empty set clears them,
which is what revokes access. On Postgres it locks the user's row so
concurrent syncs replace rather than merge, and it compares memberships
in Go byte order rather than the database collation.
PruneGroupMemberships drops a source's memberships outside a domain (or
all of them) so disabling sync or changing its domain takes effect at
startup.

User, node and pre-auth key queries preload memberships in a fixed number
of queries, so the policy manager never queries the database per group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

policy/v2: resolve identity-provider groups as group:<name>@<domain>

Resolve a group:<name>@<domain> reference that the policy does not define
to the untagged nodes of users whose identity-provider memberships include
<name>@<domain>, matched case-insensitively. This is Tailscale's syntax
for synced groups, so policies carry over unchanged.

Identity-provider groups live in their own namespace: a group the policy
defines is always resolved from its policy members, so no one who can name
a group in the identity provider can join a policy group used for tag
ownership or route approval. An undefined plain group:<name> is still
rejected; an undefined group:<name>@<domain> is valid and grants nothing
until someone is a member, failing closed. Malformed references are
rejected.

Tag ownership through such a group reads the policy manager's current
users rather than the node's copy of its user.

The alias, owner and auto-approver parsers now match the group: prefix
before the username '@' heuristic; previously any group name containing
'@' was silently parsed as a username that matched no one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

policy/v2: recompile per-node filters when their grants change

updateLocked decided whether to clear the per-node filter caches and
report a change from the global filter, tag owner, auto-approver and
exit-node hashes. Per-node grants (via and autogroup:self) are compiled
from pm.compiledGrants for each node and never appear in the global
filter, so a change affecting only them went unnoticed: a node whose
filter was cached kept a stale one, and nothing was broadcast.

A user rename that changed whom such a grant matched was already
affected; identity-provider group memberships make it the normal path
for granting and revoking access. Hash the compiled grants as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

oidc: sync the groups claim into identity-provider group memberships

With oidc.groups.enabled, each login replaces the user's OIDC group
memberships with the groups asserted in oidc.groups.claim, qualified with
oidc.groups.domain. A group removed at the identity provider, or a
missing claim, is revoked at the next login, and a login that
authenticates but is rejected by authorization (such as allowed_groups)
revokes all of them. Enabling sync without a valid domain fails config
validation.

A membership change is broadcast from the callback. The registration or
SSH check that follows finds the policy manager already updated and
reports no policy change of its own, and a user who abandons the flow
must still lose revoked groups. Only that policy delta is sent, and only
when memberships changed; the user change stays unbroadcast as before,
so a new node's registration still announces the node (#2888).

The claim may be a single string or an array, is looked up by its
literal name first (Auth0 URL claims contain dots) and then as a dotted
path into nested claims (Keycloak's realm_access.roles), and is taken
from the userinfo response when present there. A name already qualified
with the domain, as providers that name groups by email address send it,
is accepted; names that cannot be qualified are skipped with a warning.

At startup, memberships the configuration no longer grants are removed:
all of them when sync is disabled, or those outside the domain when it
changes, so neither change waits for each user to log in again. The
NodeStore's copies of a user are refreshed when their groups change, so
node responses show current groups.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

api/v1: expose users' identity-provider groups

Add groups, the qualified <name>@<domain> identity-provider groups the
user is a member of, to the v1 User response (always an array), and show
them in `headscale users list`. The generated client and the recorded
v1 responses are updated accordingly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

integration: cover OIDC group sync end to end

TestOIDCGroupsGrantAndRevokeAccess logs a user in three times against
the mock provider (no groups, a member of Engineering, no groups) under
an ACL written as group:engineering@example.com, and checks through a
connected peer's packet filter that the grant arrives without a restart
and is revoked when the provider drops the group.

TestOIDCGroupsDisabledDoesNotPersist checks that nothing is stored with
sync off, the default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: document identity-provider groups in the policy

Document oidc.groups.{enabled,claim,domain}, the group:<name>@<domain>
syntax, how synced groups stay separate from policy groups, and the
refresh-at-login model with node.expiry as the staleness bound, with
examples for the standard, custom and nested claims. Mark the feature
as supported and drop the limitation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Hey all! Just wanted to provide an update on this PR before anyone gets too far ahead. Apologies on my part for the slow turnaround getting this wrapped up over the last few months. My wife and I are welcoming our first son into the world so it's been quite busy.

That said, I'm trying to get this wrapped up this week. I found a couple of issues with my implementation that need tweaked and a few more changes are now needed after rebasing with main. That said I'm working through the updates now, a good chunk of it is already done. Hoping to get the rest of it pushed up in the next few days and be ready for review again.

Again sorry about the delays on this everyone, I know it's a desired feature right now.
